description: In aircraft manufacturing, multiple skin components need to be processed through a series of operations. In this production setting, each job (representing an aircraft skin component) must be processed according to a predefined sequence of operations. Each operation can be performed on multiple machines able to perform the step with different processing times, providing flexibility in machine selection. However, each machine can process only one operation at a time, ensuring no resource conflicts. The system automatically handles temporal rules between consecutive operations: tight rules require time gaps of 15 time units or less, while loose rules require time gaps of 30 time units or more. The goal is to make as small as possible the latest finishing time, which represents the largest completion time across all jobs, thus improving the overall production efficiency. Can you work out the best workable plan?

An inter-job precedence rule is imposed: all operations of Job 3 can only commence after all operations of Job 2 have been completed, reflecting dependencies in the manufacturing process where certain components must be fully processed before subsequent components can begin. The goal is to make as small as possible the latest finishing time, which represents the largest completion time across all jobs, thus improving the overall production efficiency. Can you work out the best workable plan?

In advanced battery management systems in electric vehicles and energy storage applications, where battery modules must be dynamically configured over multiple time periods to improve pack efficiency. The system contains several available modules in each series column, and each module can be either activated or deactivated in each period. The number of activated modules must be the same in every series column so that the parallel structure remains balanced. The pack output voltage is obtained from the selected module voltages and must stay within 95% to 105% of the nominal pack voltage. The load current is shared by the activated parallel modules, so the current through any activated module must not exceed the largest safe current of a single module. The goal is to make as small as possible total net energy loss, where activated modules contribute resistance loss and inactive modules provide an electrochemical recovery benefit. Can you work out the best workable plan?

In urban infrastructure planning, electric vehicle charging facilities must be strategically deployed to serve a growing population of EV users. In the service-placement setting, each defined demand area (such as residential zones, commercial centers, and transportation hubs) has a predicted charging demand that must be fully served to ensure adequate service coverage. Each candidate station location has a largest service capacity rule, limiting the number of users or charging events it can accommodate. The task is to choose the best subset of possible locations to activate as charging stations. The goal is to make as small as possible the combined overall cost, which includes both the sum of fixed construction costs for all activated stations and the total service cost for all users (typically based on distance or travel time), thereby achieving an economically efficient charging network layout. Can you work out the best workable plan?

In molecular biology and genetic engineering, specific DNA sequences must be designed to meet stringent biochemical rules. All designed DNA sequences must be selected from a predefined word list that contains valid nucleotide combinations, ensuring biological feasibility. The GC content, representing the proportion of guanine (G) and cytosine (C) bases, must be exactly 50% for each sequence to maintain best thermodynamic stability during molecular interactions. To ensure sequence diversity and avoid cross-hybridization issues, the Hamming distance—which measures the number of differing positions—between any two different DNA sequences must be at least 4, providing sufficient discrimination between distinct sequences. Additionally, the Hamming distance between any DNA sequence and its reverse complement must be at least 4 to prevent self-hybridization and secondary structure formation that could interfere with intended molecular functions. The design goal is to construct a set of 6 DNA sequences, each precisely 8 bases in length, that simultaneously satisfies all the above biochemical and structural rules. Can you work out the best workable plan?

In logistics and supply chain management, a fleet of three unmanned vehicles must deliver goods from a central depot to customer locations. Each customer location, except the depot and any explicitly skipped location, must be visited exactly once. Each used vehicle may leave the depot at most once, must preserve continuity of each trip at every visited customer, and returns consistently with its route. Every trip must form one connected journey rather than separate loops. The total demand assigned to each vehicle must not exceed its capacity, which is 200 units. The goal is to make as small as possible the total Euclidean travel distance of all travelled route segments. Can you work out the best workable plan?
